findings.claim: The new one-named-file exemption is `len(targets)==1 and not endswith('/') and '.' in basename`. That treats hidden CODE_ROOTS as files: `rg pattern .github` and `grep -rn foo .github` return None (allowed), while the same walk with a trailing slash still denies graft-first. `.claude` matches. The added test only covers real files (README.md, lane.conf, json); a merge to master ships a content-search walk of those code roots.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "import importlib.util,shlex,sys,tempfile; from pathlib import Path; p=Path('ops/devlane/hooks/claude/matrix.py'); sys.path.insert(0,str(p.parent)); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('m',p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); (t/'.git').mkdir(); (t/'.github/workflows').mkdir(parents=True); print('dot-github', m.graft_first(shlex.split('rg pattern .github'), str(t), str(t), 'x')); print('slash', bool(m.graft_first(shlex.split('rg pattern .github/'), str(t), str(t), 'x')))"

findings.claim: remove (and add) read-modify-write the single host-wide deliverable.json with no lock or atomic replace. Sessions on one host share that file by design. If A reads a one-branch lock and unlinks because left==[], while B's add has already written a second branch, A's unlink deletes B's in-progress lock. Two overlapping removes from a stale copy restore a branch the other session just lifted. LD-28 added remove so landing one session would not wipe the others; the racy unlink reintroduces that wipe.
